name: Riveted wrought-iron plate and angle (built-up girders and ribs)
process: Rolled wrought-iron plates, angles and tees are cut, punched or drilled, and assembled into box girders and I-section ribs; red-hot rivets are driven through the holes and headed, and shrink as they cool, pulling the plates together. Every seam carries a row of domed heads. The glazing bars and purlins are rolled sections, bolted or riveted to the ribs. Wrought iron is hand-worked by heating, hammering and rolling; it is not cast.
processSources: M. Bussell, '19th-century Structural Ironwork in Buildings: Understanding, Care and Re-use', The Building Conservation Directory (2011), https://www.buildingconservation.com/articles/structural-ironwork/structural-ironwork.htm
